_about: Route 3, the Brinewick road, and the Five that answer branch. One auto-loaded detail pack: maps, rooms, scenes, spawns, the Cobblecrest exit, the clues and Associate Quinn. The road opens once story.route3_open is set: Rook's last crates (story.rc_done) plus that side's chapter end (story.hc_council_done for the Keepers, story.gb_done for Glimmerwell). Brinewick stays shut. The five are Glimmerwell's first relays, built before the Tuning chips; the hum woke them. Names and lines are marked placeholders. Spec: handoff/walklings/ARBITER_UNITS.md.

ans_open: Lumen kept the Brinewick road dark. The road did not listen. You walked it, and you heard the hum.
My oldest page has three words on it. COUNT. GATHER. LISTEN. Then a blank, where a fourth should go.
Before the chips, Glimmerwell built five relays to do that work. The hum woke them. They walked off.
Find them. Quiet them, or keep them. Look at your own hands either way.
Start where the counting started. The old census post on Route 2.
ans_open@glimmer: You made it down the Brinewick road. Good. Your review is closed, so this is next quarter.
Before the chips, we ran a pilot. Five relays. A counter, a lamp, a crow, a tether, a wisp.
The cradle hummed and they walked off the books. Relay coverage is our proudest number. Five are missing.
Bring the units home. Nothing sharp. Nothing cold.
The census post on Route 2 is still counting. Start there. Have a bright day.
ans_clue_tallybat: An old Glow Census post. The counter clicks with nobody near it: 1, 2, 3, 4. Then it starts again.
Tally marks run off the post and down the road. Something east of here still counts, low to high.
ans_clue_dimlamp: A Comfort Lamp on a stake, set to RELAY. Beside it stands an empty stake and a cut cord.
A tag on the pole: LAMP COUNT 11 OF 12. DELIVERED BY R. The twelfth walked off toward the Brinewick road.
ans_clue_filecrow: A box of old Keeper reports. One page is new, in Mo's hand: CROW. FILES. SEEN ON THE BRINEWICK ROAD.
Under it, a RegenX folder label. Somebody filed it in the wrong archive. On purpose.
ans_clue_filecrow@glimmer: A Census file cart, parked under the trees. Its drawer is empty except for one black feather.
The sign-out sheet says: RELOCATED, BRINEWICK ROAD OFFICE. Nobody signed it.
ans_clue_cordhound: A chewed cord trails from the BRINEWICK DOCKS crates and down the open road.
Small paw prints walk beside it. They stop at every crate, then go on.
ans_clue_humwisp: The dock chart. Brinewick is circled, and its light is dark. Under it is a second light. Lit.
Nobody marked it. It sits where the Brinewick road ends, and it hums, very softly.
ans_clue_humwisp@glimmer: The cradle hums low. Its cursor spells COUNT. GATHER. LISTEN. Then a word it never printed before: ANSWER.
Under the glass, a sticky note: RELAY HOUSE. END OF THE ROAD. LEGACY.
ans_tallybat: A bat hangs from the tally gate, counting crates that are not there. It counts you. Twice.
It stops counting. It folds its wings and settles near {pet}.
The tally clicks on. It is still counting, somewhere close.
ans_dimlamp: LAMP COUNT 11 OF 12. The twelfth lamp glows between the cots and asks you to stay.
Its glow turns soft and stays soft. It follows {pet} out to the road.
The lamps dim. The room waits for another visitor.
ans_filecrow: It closes the ledger with one wing. Now it will hear you.
It closes the ledger and hops over to {pet}, light as paper.
It flips a card over: FILE PENDING.
ans_cordhound: The pup skids up, cord in its teeth. Every crate in the yard hums at once.
It drops the cord at your feet and wags once.
The cord pulls tight. The pup is back among the crates.
ans_humwisp: The relay hums so low you feel it in your teeth. A wisp drifts off the old machine and turns to you.
The hum drops to a whisper. The wisp curls beside {pet}, and the relay goes quiet.
Far off, in a box, Bitlet's cursor wakes. It types one new word: HELLO.
The wisp sinks back into the hum. The relay keeps calling.
ans_close: COUNT. GATHER. LISTEN. ANSWER. My oldest page has four words now. I wrote the last one in myself.
Their hum is smaller now. Smaller is not gone. I wrote that down too.
ans_close@glimmer: All five units accounted for. That is a very good quarter.
The cradle read came back blank this morning. No words at all. I have never seen it print nothing.
Do not ask me what that means. I would not know. Have a bright day.
ans_clue_humwisp_mast: The old mast hums. It never hummed before.
The four went quiet. The fifth got louder. It waits where the Brinewick road ends.
ans_quinn_word: Four units home. I pulled last quarter's cradle read. You should see the bottom line.
COUNT. GATHER. LISTEN. Under it, smaller, a word the cradle never printed before: ANSWER.
The fifth is at the old Relay House, where the road ends. Legacy coverage. Off the books.

ans_dim_lamp_b: You turn the lamp down. Its glow stops asking you to stay.
ans_dim_cot: The cot is warm. The lamps lean closer.
You lie down. Just for a moment.
When you open your eyes, a lamp-headed shade is at the foot of the cot.
Two lamps down. One glow is left in the room, and it is not a lamp.
You stay up. The lamps wait. They are very good at waiting.
ans_dimlamp_wait: It glows between the cots and will not look at you. It wants you to lie down first.
ans_rook_lamp: {name}? I saw the sanctuary go dark. Is that... one of the Census lamps?
Twelve lamps. I counted them onto the cart myself. I signed for eleven and never asked why.
It looks better out here. Lighter. ...Tell it I'm sorry about the cart?
ans_rook_lamp@glimmer: Hey, partner. Is that the twelfth lamp? From my delivery?
I signed for eleven. Dorian said the twelfth was a rounding error. It doesn't look like a rounding error.
...Funny. It looks happier with you than it did on the stake.
ans_file_1: A file card tucked in the ledger. CARD 1. UNIT: TALLY. STATUS: COUNTING.
ans_file_2: A file card in the cart. CARD 2. UNIT: LAMP. STATUS: RELOCATED.
ans_file_3: A file card under the chart. CARD 3. UNIT: CROW. STATUS: DECOMMISSIONED.
ans_filecrow_ask: A crow with a file-card chest perches on the ledger. It files your name, then waits.
It wants something filed back. The office is full of cards.
The crow taps the desk. One of your cards is false. It wants to know if you can tell.
FILE PENDING. It hops to a high shelf and starts a new card about you.
FILE PENDING. It hops to a high shelf and starts a new card about you.
It pecks CARD 3 and tears it neatly in two. Not decommissioned. Not yet.
ans_cordhound_dodge: A shadow pup on a cord nobody holds. It darts behind the crates when you reach for it.
By the sealed crate, the loose end of the cord twitches.
ans_cord_tug: A chewed cord, tied to nothing.
You tug. Somewhere in the yard, something tugs back.
You leave it. The cord twitches anyway.
